author: Igor Patrick
description:
China on Wednesday condemned an arrest warrant issued in the US state of Florida for former Cuban president Raul Castro over the 1996 downing of two civilian planes, accusing the United States of using the courts to pressure Havana.
Foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning was asked about the warrant by the state-run Global Times at a regular briefing in Beijing. She referred to the 95-year-old as “comrade Raul Castro”, a “venerated” leader held in high international esteem.
Mao said China opposed...
title: ‘Comrade Raul’: Beijing defends Cuba’s ex-leader over Florida murder warrant

author: Tang Meng Kit
description:
Last month, the US published the fine print of a US$686 million upgrade deal for Pakistan’s F-16 fighter jets. The deal is for data link systems, new encryption gear and a refit that keeps the jets flying until 2040. The notice says Pakistan can protect the technology to “substantially the same degree” as the US government.
The Pakistan Air Force is also the only declared interested buyer of China’s J-35 stealth fighter, a generational leap in technology.
The Chinese jet first flew at the Zhuhai...
title: Pakistan and the US factor as China looks to sell its J-35 stealth jets

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China has allowed the Philippines to resupply a grounded warship on a disputed South China Sea reef, the coastguard said on Wednesday, as tension remains high over the Chinese ambassador’s controversial comment.
The Philippines delivered necessities to its warship BRP Sierra Madre grounded at the Second Thomas Shoal on Wednesday, “with permission from the Chinese side”, the China Coast Guard said in a statement.
“The China Coast Guard conducted confirmation checks and maintained full supervision...
title: China says it allowed Philippines to resupply warship amid diplomatic tensions

author: Lucy Quaggin
description:
Just two weeks before the US midterm elections, Jim Himes, the top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee, said he did not believe America would maintain its lead over China in frontier AI indefinitely, describing restrictions on advanced chips as Washington’s key leverage.
“I don’t believe for one second that we’re going to maintain a lead over Chinese frontier models forever. But we should for as long as we can,” said Himes at a Brookings Institution event in Washington.
“And the one...
title: Top Democrat says chip restrictions are ‘key lever’ for US AI edge over China

author: Han Li,Zhang Tong
description:
Virginia Tech is accelerating the closure of a joint undergraduate programme with China’s Xidian University, bringing forward the end of a partnership that it had previously planned to keep running until 2029, according to a university spokesperson and a copy of an official letter reviewed by the South China Morning Post.
This decision comes as the Pentagon’s push to tighten oversight of US universities’ research ties with China has led to more than 80 termination-related actions across 30...
title: US colleges scale back cooperation with Chinese institutions after Pentagon’s push

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
A flight-tested attack drone similar to Iran’s Shahed model that its Taiwanese maker says could reach military targets in mainland China is meant to swamp PLA air defences, analysts said.
Drawing on battlefield lessons from Ukraine and the Middle East, military experts broadly agree on the utility of such low-cost systems but differ on how it could be deployed in a conflict with Beijing should it enter service.
While some see greater value in targeting People’s Liberation Army forces in the...
title: Taiwan’s Iran-style attack drone could swamp PLA air defences: analysts

author: Carol Yang
description:
Europe should work with Beijing to develop shipping through the Arctic rather than trying to advance its transatlantic security alliance by framing China as a threat linked to Russia.
That was the assessment of Chinese analysts following the release of the European Union’s Arctic policy on Tuesday.
In addition to identifying Russia as its main threat, the policy warns of Beijing’s growing strategic ambitions in the European Arctic through its deepening alignment with Moscow.
“With our new...
title: Is China a Russia-allied Arctic threat to Europe or a potential polar partner?

author: Hugh Harsono
description:
From October 22, China’s grace period for the disclosure and settlement of certain offshore-trust tax liabilities ends.
For the Chinese government, this deadline highlights its desire to affirm control over capital outflows, while for Chinese high-net-worth families, it serves as a reminder that it is now harder to keep international assets beyond the reach of the government.
The deadline sits against the backdrop of China tightening scrutiny around cryptocurrency, stablecoins and real-world...
title: China’s offshore tax crackdown could inadvertently fuel a digital dollar boom

author: Holly Chik
description:
In an age of AI-induced answers to complex mathematical problems, Chinese mathematician Sun Zhiwei maintains that curiosity and asking good questions are more important then ever.
Over a career spent probing the edges of number theory, Sun, a 61-year-old professor at Nanjing University’s department of mathematics, has built a vast landscape of problems – more than 1,000 and counting – for the global research community to tackle.
While traditional mathematical training emphasises mastering...
title: Chinese mathematician Sun Zhiwei proposes 1,000 problems to challenge AI

author: Xinlu Liang
description:
Beijing’s director of the Taiwan Affairs Office (TAO), Song Tao, has held a rare meeting with a delegation of US scholars that pledged to push for the peaceful development of cross-strait ties.
During the meeting in Beijing on Tuesday with a delegation from the National Committee on American Foreign Policy (NCAFP) led by its president and CEO, Susan M. Elliott, Song spoke of a broader diplomatic context following high-level summit meetings between Chinese and US leadership.
“President Xi Jinping...
title: Beijing’s top Taiwan official meets US think tank to reaffirm red lines

author: Liu Zhen
description:
China’s Type 051C destroyer Shenyang has been spotted undergoing sea trials after a reported refit, as the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) begins phasing out legacy warships following the commissioning of a massive wave of new vessels.
Witness photographs circulating on social media appear to show the Shenyang, hull number 115 and lead ship of the Type 051C class, with its Russian-made hardware replaced by domestic air defence systems.
While precise details have yet to be independently confirmed,...
title: China’s Type 051C gets a refit as the PLA Navy’s legacy warships near retirement

author: Albert Bakhtizin
description:
As turbulence grows in many countries, it is tempting to ask if there is a global hegemon that can sort everything out fairly.
US President Donald Trump has threatened that his country would not defend Nato allies if they failed to spend enough on their defence. Together with new trade barriers, his words suggest that the US is scaling back its ambitions for global leadership and concentrating more on its own region.
Our latest projections of national strength for 2027 take into account...
title: Can China turn national power into world leadership?

author: Caroline Lin
description:
As Super Typhoon Champi – now the strongest storm of the year worldwide – barrels towards eastern China, authorities are planning evacuations and urging those in its path to prepare.
Airports in major Chinese cities could be affected by the storm, including Wenzhou Longwan, Fuzhou Changle, Ningbo Lishe, Hangzhou Xiaoshan, Shanghai Hongqiao, Shanghai Pudong and Xiamen Gaoqi, according to aviation data platform VariFlight.
Travellers are bracing for potential disruptions, though there have been no...
title: Strongest storm of the year barrels towards Taiwan and mainland China

author: SCMP
description:
We have put together stories from our coverage on science from the past two weeks to help you stay informed. If you would like to see more of our reporting, please consider subscribing.
1. China breakthrough unlocks low-cost, high-margin sustainable aviation fuel
Chinese researchers have developed a catalyst that converts synthesis gas into sustainable jet fuel – an advance that could boost production, help meet net-zero carbon goals and yield a gross profit margin above 50 per cent.
2. Landmark...
title: China-US team’s ‘gold factory’ relic; next-gen diabetes care: 7 science highlights

author: Shi Huang
description:
Some 5 metres (16.4 feet) underground near one of China’s oldest cities lies the life-size army of thousands of terracotta warriors.
The purpose of the army, located 35km (22 miles) northeast of historic Xian, was to protect China’s first emperor, Qin Shi Huang, in the afterlife. The Terracotta Army was buried with him after his death in 210BC.
Now, a new study shows that a portion of the terracotta warriors was largely made by adult women and minors, not solely by men as previously...
title: Terracotta warriors could be mainly built by women and children, batch fingerprints show

author: Dannie Peng
description:
Chinese scientists have developed what they say is the world’s smallest wearable mini brain monitor that can track the activity of thousands of neurons at the same time.
Weighing in at one gram (0.35 oz), the wireless “Airscope” is the lightest device of its kind and enables researchers to track a wider range of brain activity in untethered laboratory animals.
The device was jointly developed by scientists from Tsinghua University and the Chinese PLA Medical School, and detailed in a paper...
title: China builds the world’s smallest wearable brain monitor with a cortex-wide view

author: Lawrence Chung
description:
Taiwan’s defence ministry has confirmed for the first time that it has allocated funding for the US Indo-Pacific Command to send a retired general and other personnel to observe the island’s largest annual war games.
The disclosure sheds rare official light on military exchanges that Taipei and Washington have traditionally kept out of public view, as security cooperation between the two sides deepens amid growing pressure from Beijing.
According to a defence ministry report submitted to the...
title: Taiwan admits paying for retired US general to observe largest annual war games

author: Ruairidh J. Brown
description:
Getting relations with China right is widely seen as Britain’s epoch-defining challenge. It is also one it is woefully unprepared to face.
So concluded a recent audit by the Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China (IPAC), which highlighted that top negotiators lacked basic Chinese language skills. More critically, it exposed a deeper deficit: a poor grasp of China spanning political elites and the public alike. This is rooted in a desk-bound classroom sinology rather than a nuanced appreciation...
title: Burnham’s Britain can learn from Trump in engaging with China

author: Emiliano Martínez Viademonte
description:
The family farmers who produce the lion’s share of Brazil’s staple foods are opening their arms to cutting-edge Chinese artificial intelligence in a bid to modernise operations and secure their future.
Brazil and China agreed to a five-year cooperation programme in September aimed at giving smallholders – the backbone of the Brazilian agricultural sector – an AI boost after a decade of declining employment and limited access to affordable technology.
Representatives of the Brazilian Agricultural...
title: Brazil’s family farming backbone embraces Chinese AI to reverse vital sector’s decline
